summary: Redondo Beach packs 13.3 square miles into a geography that most people underestimate — it stretches well beyond the beachfront pier and Esplanade, climbing inland through surprisingly hilly residential streets where the elevation change rewards you with unobstructed views of the Pacific and Palos Verdes Peninsula to the south. That coastal setting delivers one of Southern California's most temperate microclimates: an annual average high of 72°F with nighttime lows rarely dipping below 56°F and nine hours of daily sunshine, meaning fog burns off by mid-morning most of the year. The city sits in a genuine employment corridor — aerospace and defense contractors including Northrop Grumman's Space Park campus are literally within city limits, and the broader South Bay hosts a concentration of tech, engineering, and healthcare employers dense enough that switching jobs doesn't necessarily mean switching freeways. Still, the housing math is sobering: at a median home value of $1,225,400 against a median household income of $144,588, you're looking at a price-to-income ratio above 8:1, and even median rent at $2,562 claims a significant share of monthly take-home. The tradeoff for that cost is a city with genuine pedestrian texture — the Strand bike path connects to Hermosa and Manhattan Beach, Riviera Village offers walkable independent restaurants and shops, and the harbor area anchors a working waterfront rather than a purely decorative one. Redondo is a place where the commute might be manageable but the mortgage rarely feels that way.
